pairs: Erat autem Pascha et azyma post biduum: et quærebant summi sacerdotes et scribæ quomodo eum dolo tenerent, et occiderent.
Now the feast of Passover and of Unleavened Bread was two days away. And the leaders of the priests, and the scribes, were seeking a means by which they might deceitfully seize him and kill him.

Et cum esset Bethaniæ in domo Simonis leprosi,
And when he was in Bethania, in the house of Simon the leper,
venit mulier habens alabastrum unguenti nardi spicati pretiosi:
a woman arrived having an alabaster container of ointment, of precious spikenard.
et fracto alabastro, effudit super caput ejus.
And breaking open the alabaster container, she poured it over his head.
Erant autem quidam indigne ferentes intra semetipsos,
But there were some who became indignant within themselves
Ut quid perditio ista unguenti facta est?
“What is the reason for this waste of the ointment?
poterat enim unguentum istud venundari plus quam trecentis denariis,
For this ointment could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii
and been given to the poor.”
What is the reason that you trouble her?
Bonum opus operata est in me:
She has done a good deed for me.
For the poor, you have with you always.
you are able to do good to them.
But you do not have me always.
But she has done what she could.
prævenit ungere corpus meum in sepulturam.
She has arrived in advance to anoint my body for burial.
Ubicumque prædicatum fuerit Evangelium istud in universo mundo,
wherever this Gospel shall be preached throughout the entire world,
the things she has done also shall be told,
went away, to the leaders of the priests,
in order to betray him to them.
And they, upon hearing it, were gladdened.
et promiserunt ei pecuniam se daturos.
And they promised him that they would give him money.
Et quærebat quomodo illum opportune traderet.
And he sought an opportune means by which he might betray him.
Et primo die azymorum quando Pascha immolabant,
And on the first day of Unleavened Bread,
et paremus tibi ut manduces Pascha?
“Where do you want us to go and prepare for you to eat the Passover?”
Et mittit duos ex discipulis suis,
And he sent two of his disciples,
et occurret vobis homo lagenam aquæ bajulans:
And you will meet a man carrying a pitcher of water;
And wherever he will have entered,
say to the owner of the house,
ubi Pascha cum discipulis meis manducem?
where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?’
Et ipse vobis demonstrabit cœnaculum grande,
And he will show you a large cenacle, fully furnished.
you shall prepare it for us.”
And they found it just as he had told them.
And while reclining and eating with them at table,
quia unus ex vobis tradet me,
But they began to be sorrowful and to say to him,
qui intingit mecum manum in catino.
who dips his hand with me in the dish.
Et Filius quidem hominis vadit sicut scriptum est de eo:
And indeed, the Son of man goes, just as it has been written of him.
væ autem homini illi per quem Filius hominis tradetur!
But woe to that man by whom the Son of man will be betrayed.
bonum erat ei, si non esset natus homo ille.
It would be better for that man if he had never been born.”

giving thanks, he gave it to them.
And they all drank from it.
Hic est sanguis meus novi testamenti,
“This is my blood of the new covenant,
which shall be shed for many.
quia jam non bibam de hoc genimine vitis usque in diem illum,
that I will no longer drink from this fruit of the vine,
cum illud bibam novum in regno Dei.
until that day when I will drink it new in the kingdom of God.”
Et hymno dicto exierunt in montem Olivarum.
And having sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Omnes scandalizabimini in me in nocte ista:
“You will all fall away from me in this night.
and the sheep will be scattered.’
But after I have risen again,
I will go before you to Galilee.”
Et si omnes scandalizati fuerint in te,
“Even if all will have fallen away from you,
quia tu hodie in nocte hac,
that this day, in this night,
before the rooster has uttered its voice twice,
you will deny me three times.”
Et si oportuerit me simul commori tibi,
“Even if I must die along with you,
And they all spoke similarly also.
And they went to a country estate,
And he said to his disciples,
And he began to be afraid and wearied.
Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem:
And when he had proceeded on a little ways,
he fell prostrate on the ground.
the hour might pass away from him.
all things are possible to you.
But let it be, not as I will,
Were you not able to be vigilant for one hour?
so that you may not enter into temptation.
And going away again, he prayed,
denuo invenit eos dormientes (erant enim oculi eorum gravati),
he found them sleeping yet again,
(for their eyes were heavy) and they did not know how to respond to him.
Et venit tertio, et ait illis:
And he arrived for the third time,
ecce Filius hominis tradetur in manus peccatorum.
Behold, the Son of man will be betrayed into the hands of sinners.
he who will betray me is near.”
And while he was still speaking,
venit Judas Iscariotes unus de duodecim,
et cum eo turba multa cum gladiis
and with him was a large crowd with swords and clubs,
sent from the leaders of the priests,
Dederat autem traditor ejus signum eis,
Now his betrayer had given them a sign,
At illi manus injecerunt in eum,
But they laid hands on him
Unus autem quidam de circumstantibus educens gladium,
Then a certain one of those standing near,
struck a servant of the high priest and cut off his ear.
And in response, Jesus said to them:
Tamquam ad latronem existis cum gladiis et lignis comprehendere me?
“Have you set out to apprehend me, just as if to a robber, with swords and clubs?
quotidie eram apud vos in templo docens,
Daily, I was with you in the temple teaching,
and you did not take hold of me.
But in this way, the scriptures are fulfilled.”
Then his disciples, leaving him behind,
Adolescens autem quidam sequebatur eum amictus sindone super nudo:
Now a certain young man followed him, having nothing but a fine linen cloth over himself.
And they took hold of him.
But he, rejecting the fine linen cloth,
Et adduxerunt Jesum ad summum sacerdotem:
And they led Jesus to the high priest.
Petrus autem a longe secutus est eum usque intro in atrium summi sacerdotis:
But Peter followed him from a distance,
et sedebat cum ministris ad ignem,
even into the court of the high priest.
And he sat with the servants at the fire and warmed himself.
Summi vero sacerdotes et omne concilium quærebant adversus Jesum testimonium ut eum morti traderent:
Yet truly, the leaders of the priests and the entire council sought testimony against Jesus, so that they might deliver him to death,
Multi enim testimonium falsum dicebant adversus eum:
For many spoke false testimony against him,
but their testimony did not agree.
rising up, bore false witness against him,
Ego dissolvam templum hoc manu factum,
‘I will destroy this temple, made with hands,
et per triduum aliud non manu factum ædificabo.
and within three days I will build another, not made with hands.’”
Et non erat conveniens testimonium illorum.
And their testimony did not agree.
Et exsurgens summus sacerdos in medium,
And the high priest, rising up in their midst,
dicens: Non respondes quidquam ad ea quæ tibi objiciuntur ab his?
“Do you have nothing to say in answer to the things that are brought against you by these ones?”
Ille autem tacebat, et nihil respondit.
But he was silent and gave no answer. Again,
the high priest questioned him, and he said to him,
et dixit ei: Tu es Christus Filius Dei benedicti?
“Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed God?”
et videbitis Filium hominis sedentem a dextris virtutis Dei,
And you shall see the Son of man sitting at the right hand of the power of God
and arriving with the clouds of heaven.”
Summus autem sacerdos scindens vestimenta sua,
Then the high priest, rending his garments,
How does it seem to you?”
Qui omnes condemnaverunt eum esse reum mortis.
And they all condemned him, as guilty unto death.
And some began to spit on him,
and to strike him with fists,
And the servants struck him with the palms their hands.
Et cum esset Petrus in atrio deorsum,
And while Peter was in the court below,
venit una ex ancillis summi sacerdotis:
one of the maidservants of the high priest arrived.
et cum vidisset Petrum calefacientem se,
And when she had seen Peter warming himself,
Et tu cum Jesu Nazareno eras.
“You also were with Jesus of Nazareth.”
“I neither know nor understand what you saying.”
Rursus autem cum vidisset illum ancilla,
Then again, when a maidservant had seen him,
she began to say to the bystanders,
Et post pusillum rursus qui astabant, dicebant Petro:
And after a little while, again those standing near said to Peter:
“In truth, you are one of them.
For you, too, are a Galilean.”
Then he began to curse and to swear,
“For I do not know this man,
And immediately the rooster crowed again.
Et recordatus est Petrus verbi quod dixerat ei Jesus:
And Peter remembered the word that Jesus had said to him,
you will deny me three times.”
